structures.name: Heart
structures.function: Pumps blood through the pulmonary and systemic circulations; produces atrial natriuretic peptide (ANP) for fluid homeostasis
structures.location: Middle mediastinum, enclosed in pericardium; 2/3 to the left of midline; base at the level of T5-T8 posteriorly; apex at 5th intercostal space, midclavicular line
structures.bloodSupply: Left coronary artery (LAD + circumflex), right coronary artery
structures.innervation: Sympathetic (cardiac accelerator): T1-T5. Parasympathetic: vagus nerve (CN X). Sensory pain: T1-T4 (referred to left arm, jaw, neck)
structures.clinicalNotes: Cardiac tamponade: blood in pericardium compresses heart (Beck's triad: hypotension, muffled heart sounds, raised JVP). Dextrocardia: heart on right side. Referred cardiac pain T1-T4 explains arm and jaw pain in MI.

structures.name: Ascending Aorta
structures.function: Carries oxygenated blood from the left ventricle; gives rise to coronary arteries from aortic sinuses
structures.location: Begins at the aortic valve (T6 vertebral level), ascends to the right, continues as aortic arch at the sternal angle
structures.innervation: Aortic body chemoreceptors, baroreceptors in aortic arch
structures.clinicalNotes: Aortic dissection: Stanford Type A involves ascending aorta (surgical emergency). Aortic aneurysm: ascending > 5.5 cm is indication for surgery. Aortic coarctation narrows below ductus arteriosus.

structures.name: Pulmonary Trunk
structures.function: Carries deoxygenated blood from right ventricle to pulmonary circulation; divides into right and left pulmonary arteries at T4-5 level
structures.location: Emerges from right ventricle, ascends to the left of the ascending aorta, bifurcates beneath the aortic arch at the level of the sternal angle
structures.clinicalNotes: Saddle pulmonary embolism: large embolus straddles bifurcation causing acute right heart failure. Pulmonary hypertension: mean PA pressure >25 mmHg. Eisenmenger syndrome: reversal of left-to-right shunt due to pulmonary hypertension.

structures.name: Left Lung
structures.function: Gas exchange; 2 lobes (upper and lower) separated by oblique fissure; smaller than right due to cardiac notch; lingula corresponds to right middle lobe
structures.location: Left pleural cavity; root at T5-T7; cardiac notch on anterior surface accommodates the heart; apex extends 2.5 cm above the clavicle
structures.bloodSupply: Left pulmonary artery; bronchial arteries for lung parenchyma
structures.innervation: Pulmonary plexus: vagus (CN X) and sympathetic T2-T5
structures.clinicalNotes: Left-sided pneumothorax: needle decompression at 2nd intercostal space, midclavicular line. Pneumonia consolidation detected by dullness to percussion and bronchial breathing. Lung cancer: left upper lobe proximity to recurrent laryngeal nerve causes hoarseness.

structures.name: Right Lung
structures.function: Gas exchange; 3 lobes (upper, middle, lower) separated by oblique and horizontal fissures; larger than left
structures.location: Right pleural cavity; root at T5-T7; indented superiorly by azygos vein, anteriorly by superior vena cava and right atrium
structures.innervation: Pulmonary plexus: vagus (CN X) and sympathetic T2-T5
structures.clinicalNotes: Foreign bodies tend to enter the right main bronchus (wider, shorter, more vertical). Right lower lobe most common site of aspiration pneumonia in upright patient. Right-sided pleural effusion may compress lung causing ipsilateral dullness to percussion.

structures.name: Diaphragm
structures.function: Primary muscle of respiration; separates thoracic and abdominal cavities; has three major openings for IVC (T8), oesophagus (T10), and aorta (T12)
structures.location: Dome-shaped musculotendinous partition; right dome at T8, left dome at T9; central tendon forms aponeurotic centre
structures.innervation: Phrenic nerve C3-C5 (motor and sensory). Peripheral sensory: lower 6 intercostal nerves (referred pain to shoulder from C3-5 dermatome)
structures.clinicalNotes: Phrenic nerve injury (C3-C5): ipsilateral diaphragm paralysis seen as elevated hemidiaphragm. Right dome higher than left (liver beneath). Hiatus hernia: stomach herniation through oesophageal hiatus (most common — sliding type). Diaphragmatic hernia: neonates commonly Bochdalek type (posterior left).

structures.name: Oesophagus
structures.function: Muscular tube transporting food from pharynx to stomach; peristaltic contractions propel bolus; has upper and lower oesophageal sphincters
structures.location: Posterior mediastinum; begins at C6 (inferior border of cricoid), descends behind trachea, deviates left, passes through diaphragm at T10, joins stomach at T11 (cardia)
structures.bloodSupply: Inferior thyroid artery (upper 1/3), bronchial/oesophageal branches of aorta (middle 1/3), left gastric artery (lower 1/3)
structures.innervation: Upper 1/3: recurrent laryngeal nerve (somatic). Middle and lower: vagus plexus (parasympathetic). Sympathetic: T5-T10
structures.clinicalNotes: Three physiological constrictions: UO sphincter (C6), aortic arch + left main bronchus (T4-5), diaphragm (T10). Boerhaave syndrome: spontaneous full-thickness rupture (Mackler triad: vomiting + chest pain + subcutaneous emphysema). Barrett's oesophagus: metaplasia from GORD → oesophageal adenocarcinoma risk.

structures.name: Thoracic Duct
structures.function: Main lymphatic duct; drains all of the body except right upper quadrant; carries chyle (lymph + dietary fat) from gut
structures.location: Begins at cisterna chyli at L1-L2; enters thorax through aortic hiatus (T12); ascends right of midline between aorta and azygos vein; crosses to left at T5; arches over left subclavian artery to drain into junction of left internal jugular and subclavian veins
structures.clinicalNotes: Chylothorax: thoracic duct injury (trauma, surgery, malignancy) → milky pleural effusion with high triglycerides. Damaged during left neck dissection or oesophagectomy. Right duct drains only right upper quadrant of body.

structures.name: Left Vagus Nerve
structures.function: Parasympathetic innervation of thoracic and abdominal viscera; motor to laryngeal muscles via recurrent laryngeal nerve; forms oesophageal plexus
structures.location: Descends in carotid sheath, crosses aortic arch anteriorly, gives off left recurrent laryngeal nerve which loops under the ligamentum arteriosum, then forms the oesophageal plexus
structures.clinicalNotes: Left recurrent laryngeal nerve has longer intrathoracic course than right — compressed by aortic aneurysm, lung cancer, mediastinal lymphadenopathy causing hoarseness (Ortner syndrome). Vagotomy used historically for peptic ulcer disease.

structures.name: Intercostal Nerve (T6)
structures.function: Motor to intercostal and abdominal muscles; sensory to parietal pleura, pericardium, skin of anterior chest and abdomen (T7-11 extend onto anterior abdominal wall)
structures.location: Ventral rami of thoracic spinal nerves T1-T11; run in the intercostal groove on the inferior border of each rib (VAN order: vein, artery, nerve from superior to inferior)
structures.bloodSupply: Posterior intercostal arteries (from thoracic aorta), anterior intercostal arteries (from internal thoracic artery)
structures.clinicalNotes: Needle/drain insertion: at superior border of rib below the space (or lower quarter of space) to avoid the neurovascular bundle. Intercostal nerve block for rib fractures. Herpes zoster follows dermatomal distribution of a single intercostal nerve.

structures.name: Azygos Vein
structures.function: Drains the posterior thoracic wall and posterior mediastinum; collateral pathway between superior and inferior vena cava (IVC/SVC collateral)
structures.location: Ascends on the right side of the vertebral column in the posterior mediastinum; arches over the right lung root at T4 to drain into the superior vena cava
structures.clinicalNotes: SVC obstruction (from malignancy) → collateral drainage via azygos → engorged superficial veins on chest wall. Azygos continuation of IVC in IVC agenesis. Azygos fissure on CXR: normal variant, azygos vein in incomplete fissure of right upper lobe.

structures.name: Right Phrenic Nerve
structures.function: Sole motor supply to the right hemidiaphragm; sensory to pericardium, mediastinal and diaphragmatic pleura, and central diaphragm peritoneum
structures.location: Arises from C3-C5 in the neck; descends anterior to scalenus anterior, enters thorax, runs on the right side of the mediastinum (anterior to lung root) between the pericardium and mediastinal pleura, pierces the diaphragm with the IVC at T8
structures.bloodSupply: Pericardiophrenic artery (branch of internal thoracic artery)
structures.clinicalNotes: C3,4,5 keeps the diaphragm alive. Injury during cardiac surgery, LIMA harvest, or central venous catheterisation → ipsilateral diaphragm paralysis (elevated hemidiaphragm on CXR, sniff test positive). Sub-diaphragmatic pathology (abscess, ruptured ectopic) → referred pain to ipsilateral shoulder tip.
